title: kk7.3: CORS layer wired into build_router()
description:
What: Add configurable CORS middleware to build_router() in crates/mail/src/server.rs using tower-http CorsLayer.

Algorithm:
1. In build_router(state: Arc<AppState>), read state.cors (or pass CorsConfig directly):
   - Add cors_config: Arc<CorsConfig> to AppState (or read from state.base_url pattern)
   Actually: read config from state. Simplest: add pub cors: CorsConfig to AppState, populated from Config::cors in run_server().
2. Build the CorsLayer:
   - If cors_config.enabled is false: add no layer (identity layer / no-op)
   - If cors_config.enabled is true:
     a. If allowed_origins contains "*": use CorsLayer::permissive()
     b. Otherwise: use CorsLayer::new()
          .allow_origin(AllowOrigin::list(parsed_origins))
          .allow_methods([Method::GET, Method::POST, Method::DELETE, Method::OPTIONS])
          .allow_headers([header::AUTHORIZATION, header::CONTENT_TYPE])
          .expose_headers([HeaderName::from_static("x-usenet-ipfs-cid"), HeaderName::from_static("x-usenet-ipfs-root-cid")])
3. Apply the layer: Router::new().[...].layer(cors_layer)
4. Wire GET / to landing::landing_page handler before the CORS layer.

SECURITY INVARIANT: Never emit Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true when allow_origin is "*". The code must not set allow_credentials if origins contains "*".

Defensive programming:
- Parse each origin string to axum::http::HeaderValue; if parsing fails, log error and skip that origin
- If enabled=true but allowed_origins is empty: log warn and treat as disabled (do not allow all origins)
- No unwrap() in origin parsing

Tests: covered by kk7.4 (test bead).
Acceptance: cargo test --package usenet-ipfs-mail passes; CORS headers appear on responses with Origin header.
